title: Request Echoes: Annotated Customer Stories + Probe Listing (Dec 2028)
body:
TL;DR
- This is a compact, annotated roll-up of recent customer threads (Nov 15 - Nov 28, 2028) focused on runtime frictions, rollout safety, and KV/prefix cache behavior.
- Goal: produce 4 small probes (2 low-risk, 2 medium-effort) we can ship quickly to reduce CS escalations and provide measurable improvement signals.
- Status: collecting engineering feasibility notes; want eng review (SRE + Serving Runtime) by 2028-12-07.

Method & sources
- Sources: support tickets (top 60 by severity), 3 customer calls (acct: AtlasHealth, FinPilot, RetailSpark), Slack threads #cs-runtime, #prod-incidents, GitHub issue cross-references.
- Annotation style: each customer story below includes: summary, quote, current workaround, suggested probe.
- Quick note: I'm prioritizing symptomatic asks (observable errors/latency/consistency) over feature wishlist.

Key themes (ranked by frequency)
1) Transient KV-cache desyncs on canary rollouts — customers see partial context (esp. long chat sessions). Repro rate ~18% in calls.
2) Sudden tail-latency spikes when autoscaling triggers cold-model-instance fetch (Dedicated pools with burst enabled).
3) Request-rate routing surprises: unexpected fallbacks to cheaper model variant cause quality regressions in edge cases.
4) Hard-to-observe billing spikes when users do short bursts of high-token streaming (cost surprise).
5) Confusing rollout controls in Console for multi-model route policies — customers accidentally created overlapping policies.

Representative annotated stories
- AtlasHealth (mid-market, healthcare)
  - Summary: multi-turn assistant used in clinical note summarization. On small canary rollout they observed truncated context after ~20 turns.
  - Quote: "Context just disappears mid-conversation; we lost notes for a whole patient."
  - Workaround: forced traffic split to 100% pinned older model; rollback took 45min + manual key rotation.
  - Suggested probe: Add a tiny telemetry flag to canary responses to assert KV-cache sequence ids and expose mismatch signal in Console traces (low effort).

- FinPilot (enterprise fintech)
  - Summary: bursty nightly reconciliation jobs cause sudden model-instance fetches; observed latency 3–8x SLA during spikes.
  - Quote: "We thought we hit a regional outage — but capacity was there; instances were simply cold."
  - Workaround: pre-warm reserved capacity during runs (manual), or schedule jobs off-peak.
  - Suggested probe: experiment with short-lived pre-warm windows (configurable in Dedicated) + measure cost delta (medium effort, clear metrics).

- RetailSpark (scale SaaS)
  - Summary: deployed route with fallback to a quantized variant for cost-saving; some queries started returning lower-quality outputs for localized product names.
  - Quote: "The cheaper model mangled SKU names — shoppers got weird descriptions."
  - Workaround: tightened routing rules to never fallback for specific route tags.
  - Suggested probe: add a per-route quality guardrail that forbids fallback for routes containing known entities (low effort).

- Boutique AI agency (startup)
  - Summary: customers confused by Console rollout UI — created overlapping rollout that resulted in 3x token usage at peak.
  - Quote: "We didn't realize our canary was additive, not replace — cost shot up overnight."
  - Workaround: CS manual rollback + credits.
  - Suggested probe: Clarify labels + add a small modal explaining additive vs replacement rollout behavior (UX copy + one-line code sample) (low effort).

Ask catalog (annotated, prioritized)
- Probe A: Canary KV mismatch telemetry (Impact: high, Effort: low). Surface sequence-id diffs in traces + per-request flag for debugging. Owner: eng-serv-runtime. Linked: JIRA CS-1423.
- Probe B: Dedicated pre-warm scheduling (Impact: medium-high, Effort: medium). Add API/Console toggle for scheduled pre-warm windows. Owner: infra + dedicated product. Linked: CORE-2981.
- Probe C: Route-level fallback guardrails (Impact: medium, Effort: low). Allow blacklisting of fallback variants per route. Owner: product-hosted-api + serving runtime.
- Probe D: Rollout UX modal + cost-warning (Impact: medium, Effort: low). Small console change + telemetry to flag additive rollouts in billing dashboards. Owner: product-console + growth.

Quick impact/cost notes
- A and C can likely reduce high-severity CS escalations by ~30% (est). Return-on-effort high because fixes are detection + config, not heavy infra.
- B reduces tail-latency but may increase unit cost if overdone; recommend experiment with 1-week A/B to measure unit-cost delta.
- D is immediate: copy + modal avoids repeat mistakes; measurable by reduced rollback requests in support queue.

Open questions / unknowns (for eng review)
- Is adding a per-request debugging flag for KV-seq-id safe for PII/compliance? Ask security.
- Can we expose per-request cost-estimates for streaming in Console? Might need billing pipeline changes.
- What telemetry sampling rate is sufficient to catch KV desyncs without adding noise?

Immediate next steps (owner + ETA)
- 2028-12-05: Eng review meeting scheduled with serving-runtime + infra (Ravi + Ben) — agenda: feasibility of Probe A/B. (Owner: Ava)
- 2028-12-07: Prototype spec for Probe A (one-pager) submitted to CORE-2981. (Owner: Ravi)
- 2028-12-12: UX copy + modal mock for Rollout warning (Probe D) — ship staging. (Owner: Sofia)

Notes-to-self / loose ends
- Add anonymized session extract for AtlasHealth to linked artifacts for incident RCA (remove PHI).
- Reconcile billing-sample from RetailSpark with finance (Ben).
- Cross-check fallback behaviour with model-catalog team: which variants are flagged as 'compatible' for graceful fallback?

Slack references / where I pulled threads
- #cs-runtime: threads on 2028-11-21 "kv mismatch" (message ids: 9872–9878)
- #prod-incidents: FinPilot latency thread 2028-11-23
- Internal note: see confluence page above for raw ticket ids + call recordings.

Bottom line
- We have small, actionable probes that are low friction and map tightly to customer pain. Prioritize telemetry (Probe A) + rollout UX (Probe D) first — they unblock debugging and prevent repeat incidents.
- Probe B and C follow once feasibility / cost tradeoffs are clear.
